title: Two-Dimensional and Three-Dimensional Transforms
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of two-dimensional and three-dimensional transforms.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.
Verify the expected result and identify a common failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on two-dimensional and three-dimensional transforms and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Two-Dimensional and Three-Dimensional Transforms matters because interface appearance should reflect actual state while remaining understandable to keyboard, touch and assistive-technology users.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Transform combinations; Perspective; Three-dimensional rotation; Transform-style behavior; Understanding browser rendering differences. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.expected_output: A required email field is explicitly labeled and keeps a visible focus state.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to two-dimensional and three-dimensional transforms, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating two-dimensional and three-dimensional transforms. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to two-dimensional and three-dimensional transforms.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to two-dimensional and three-dimensional transforms.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: A required email field is explicitly labeled and keeps a visible focus state.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying two-dimensional and three-dimensional transforms without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Two-Dimensional and Three-Dimensional Transforms is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
